_doc: PRE-REGISTERED spec for FAVORABLE-EXTREME-ENTRY, per J's 2026-07-17 ~18:46 ET breakthrough directive after the 14:03 bollinger_squeeze PUT win (+$105): the fill landed at the TOP of the 14:00-14:05 bar's $0.47 upper wick (O=744.60 H=745.10 L=744.38 C=744.63), buying the put cheap right before SPY rolled to a 743.23 close. 'that is a PRIMO entry -- we need that every time it presents itself.' CRITICAL HONESTY FRAME (per task instruction): today's wick-fill was PARTLY INCIDENTAL -- the 1-min heartbeat tick happened to evaluate mid-spike; the engine did not deliberately target the wick. This prereg splits the question in two: (A) an OBSERVATIONAL characterization of ALL real engine fills (does entry LOCATION empirically correlate with outcome -- correlational on incidental fills, NOT causal, stated explicitly), and (B) a pre-registered CAUSAL A/B test of a DELIBERATE favorable-extreme resting-entry mechanism built on entry_manager.py (T-W5)'s already-tested EntryState/plan_entry_action state machine, reusing the SAME cancel-on-break watcher concept pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17 (KILLED, same day, sibling study) needed to survive adverse selection. STUDY ONLY -- no live code, no orders, no engine edits. Runner: backtest/tools/favorable_extreme_entry_study.py.
standing_doctrine: Burden of proof is on the CANDIDATE mechanism (CLAUDE.md Rule 1 / OP-16 eval-first). One exemplar fill is NOT evidence a deliberate targeting mechanism is profitable -- part (A) establishes whether location correlates with outcome AT ALL across the real fill population (precondition for (B) mattering); part (B) is the actual pre-registered 5-gate + BH-FDR test of whether DELIBERATELY targeting that location beats the status quo marketable entry, net of the adverse-selection cost a resting order structurally carries (pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17's own central finding: 74-81% raw slice-through share on a structurally similar resting-limit mechanism). Kill = current marketable-entry-on-confirmed-trigger semantics stand; a null or 'location matters but targeting doesn't' result is a valid, honestly-reported outcome (OP-22), not a failure.

exemplar.outcome: +$105, day's 2nd-best trade (verified analysis/daily-brief/2026-07-17-safe-tape-audit.md; the trade is ALSO the SAFE-TRADES-CSV-JOURNALING-GAP item -- missing from journal/trades.csv, present in core-decisions.jsonl extra_exec + fills-ledger.jsonl only)
exemplar.honesty_note: The fill landed near the bar's HIGH (top of the upper wick against a PUT/short) because the 1-min heartbeat tick happened to sample SPY mid-spike, not because any code targeted the wick. This is the INCIDENTAL fact the whole study interrogates.

motivating_context.relationship_to_pong_resting_limit_study: DIFFERENT MECHANISM, same day's family. PONG (KILLED both accounts, 4/5 gates, fails anchor_no_regression; 74.1%/81.4% raw slice-through share Safe/Bold) tests a resting order ARMED BEFORE any confirmation trigger fires, priced off a chart LEVEL via delta-mapping, competing against the engine's current semantics on level-touch episodes the engine might never even trade. THIS study tests a narrower, later-stage mechanism: on a signal the engine WOULD ALREADY TRADE (a real confirmation trigger has fired), instead of converting to a marketable fill immediately, rest a SHORT patience-window limit at a modest discount off the signal's own quoted premium (entry_manager.py's EXISTING delta-fraction convention, signal_premium*(1-delta), NOT a level-derived price) hoping the SAME kind of live-tick noise that produced today's wick fill resolves favorably before the patience window expires -- with a SPY-side cancel-watcher (reusing PONG's own concept) so a real breakout does not get chased. PONG's kill does not pre-judge this study: PONG's adverse-selection problem was structural to arming BEFORE any trigger (resting at a level the market may simply run through); this study only rests AFTER a trigger has already confirmed direction, which changes the base rate of 'was this a real move or a wick' the resting order is exposed to.

This study reuses plan_entry_action VERBATIM (imported, not re-derived) for the candidate's fill/convert/miss state transitions -- the delta_band grid brackets the shadow default (0.05/0.10/0.15).

pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17 (KILLED, same day) already built and validated a cancel-watcher concept: while a resting order is pending, if the underlying trades through the anchor level by >= a threshold before the option fills, cancel immediately rather than let the order fill into a real breakout. Its no_cancel control cell measured raw adverse selection at 74.1% (Safe) / 81.4% (Bold) slice-through share, and every cancel threshold tested (0.15/0.30/0.50) roughly halved fill count while RAISING per-trade expectancy -- direct evidence that a cancel-watcher is worth carrying into this study rather than omitting it.

The frozen ab_delta_per_trade_v2026_07_16 WF form (Fable, 2026-07-16, AMENDMENT 1) is the current house standard for any A/B ratification: delta_i = pnl_candidate(episode_i) - pnl_control(episode_i) over the union of episodes either side traded; gates = oos_positive, wf_delta>=0.70 (when is_delta_mean>0), sub_window_stable, anchor_no_regression, bh_fdr_survivor.

Round-trip PnL computed DIRECTLY from fills-ledger's own buy/sell price legs per (arm, symbol) FIFO group -- REAL broker dollars, no friction model needed (it is already priced into the fills).
population.secondary_lower_confidence: journal/trades.csv rows (167, back to 2026-04-29) that do NOT have a fills-ledger/core-decisions match (pre-dates heartbeat_core.py's 2026-06-25 earliest coverage, or a manual/webull fill) -- favorability computed from the entry bar's OWN CLOSE as a bar-close proxy for spot (no live-tick data exists for these), reported SEPARATELY and labeled match_quality='bar_proxy' vs the primary population's match_quality='decision_log' (live-tick). Never blended into the primary population's headline numbers (C7 -- distinct-confidence populations stay distinct).
population.window: 2026-06-26 through 2026-07-17 (primary, fills-ledger coverage) + 2026-04-29 through 2026-07-17 (secondary, trades.csv coverage).

favorability_metric.definition: For the entry bar B (the real-time SPY 5m bar covering the fill timestamp, from the appropriate spy_5m master), let spot = the live-tick SPY value (decision-log 'spy' field for the primary population; bar CLOSE for the secondary/proxy population). bar_range = B.high - B.low (episodes with bar_range <= 0.01 are excluded and counted, not imputed -- flat/illiquid bar, C7). favorability = (spot - B.low) / bar_range for PUT/short entries (favorable = spot near the bar HIGH, i.e. bought the put while SPY was still elevated, before the drop -- matches the exemplar exactly); favorability = (B.high - spot) / bar_range for CALL/long entries (favorable = spot near the bar LOW). Clipped to [0,1] (a live-tick sample can fall fractionally outside [B.low,B.high] at bar-boundary timing edges; clip-and-flag, not drop).

buckets.favorable_extreme: favorability >= 0.70 (top/bottom 30% of the bar's range, matching direction)
buckets.adverse_extreme: favorability <= 0.30 (bottom/top 30% of the bar's range, WRONG side)

wick_against_signal_flag.definition: True if the entry bar has a wick against the signal direction meeting the house wick-rejection threshold (backtest.lib.filters.detect_wick_rejection_bearish/detect_wick_reclaim_bullish's OWN frozen defaults, reused unchanged, not re-derived): min_wick_pct_of_range=0.50 AND min_wick_dollars=0.15. Upper wick = B.high - max(B.open, B.close) for PUT/short; lower wick = min(B.open, B.close) - B.low for CALL/long.
wick_against_signal_flag.caught_flag: True if favorability >= 0.70 AND wick_against_signal_flag is True (i.e., the fill actually landed IN that wick's zone, not just 'a wick existed somewhere in the bar') -- this is the exact exemplar pattern.

part_a_characterization.reporting: A favorability-bucket x outcome table (n, mean $pnl, win rate) for the primary population, the secondary population shown separately, and the wick-caught subset highlighted. Given the primary population's likely small n (dozens, not hundreds), NO significance/gate claim is attached here -- pure descriptive evidence, explicitly labeled thin-n and correlational, feeding the judgment of whether part (B) is worth having run (a precondition check, not itself a ratification gate).

part_b_deliberate_mechanism._doc: PRE-REGISTERED CAUSAL A/B. The actual breakthrough test: does DELIBERATELY resting for a short window at a discount off the signal premium (instead of converting immediately to a marketable fill) beat the status quo, net of the adverse-selection cost (missed clean runners the resting order never caught) that pong-resting-limit already proved is real on a structurally similar mechanism?

hypothesis.statement: On a REAL confirmation-trigger signal (the SAME detection the current engine uses: detect_level_rejection/detect_wick_rejection_bearish for PUT, detect_level_reclaim/detect_wick_reclaim_bullish for CALL), replacing the current immediate marketable-ish entry with a short-patience resting limit at signal_premium*(1-delta_band) (entry_manager.EntryState/plan_entry_action, policy in {cancel, convert} on patience exhaustion), GATED by a SPY-side cancel-watcher that cancels the resting order outright if the underlying trades through the signal's own trigger level by >= cancel_threshold before the option fills -- produces positive-expectancy entries under SS-B-lineage exit shapes and honest non-double-counted friction, on the delta population versus the CURRENT engine's immediate marketable-entry semantics, for at least one (delta_band, policy, cancel_threshold) cell on at least one account.
hypothesis.falsifiable_prediction: If TRUE: at least one of the 18 cells' delta population clears all 5 ratification gates + BH-FDR on Safe and/or Bold. If FALSE: no cell clears on either account -- KILL, current immediate-entry semantics stand. Per the task's explicit framing, a FALSE result that nonetheless shows part (A)'s location correlation is real is reported as 'location matters, but this deliberate targeting mechanism does not capture it profitably' -- a genuinely different, still-honest finding from 'location never mattered at all', and the scorecard distinguishes the two explicitly.

mechanism_spec.signal_population: IDENTICAL detection + scoping to pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17's own control_outcome(): per day, the SAME as-of-causal level set (backtest.lib.levels._detect_from_history, frozen at 09:30 ET first bar, reused unchanged via direct import of pong_resting_limit_study's build_level_by_day/_detect_from_history -- NOT re-derived) with role assignment (support=CALL if L < day_open_spot, resistance=PUT otherwise); for EVERY (date, level, role) combination, scan RTH bars 09:35 ET onward for the FIRST bar where the appropriate trigger fires (detect_level_rejection or detect_wick_rejection_bearish for PUT; detect_level_reclaim or detect_wick_reclaim_bullish for CALL), matching pong_resting_limit_study.py's control_outcome() function VERBATIM (imported and called directly, not reimplemented) -- this is the SAME proxy for 'what the current engine would trade' both sibling studies today rely on.
mechanism_spec.signal_premium_anchor: ctrl['entry_premium_raw'] from control_outcome() -- the first option bar's OPEN at/after (trigger_ts + 5min), the house 'fill price' convention (ribbon_ride_strike_exit_ab.fetch_entry_and_bars). This value is BOTH the control's own marketable entry price (unchanged, full house entry-side friction applied) AND the candidate's EntryState.from_signal(signal_premium=...) anchor -- the two arms start from the identical observed price, differing only in HOW they convert that observation into a fill.

candidate_state_machine.core: automation/state/fleet/entry_manager.py EntryState.from_signal + plan_entry_action, imported and called UNCHANGED (no re-derivation) -- the same module T-W5 already unit-tested for exact parity against the validated backtest reference t3_entry_matrix.entry_fill.
candidate_state_machine.tick_discretization: ONE plan_entry_action() call per subsequent 5-min OPRA option bar (walk_bars from control_outcome(), the same real-OPRA local-cache bars the control's own exit replay uses) -- ask=bar.low is the tick's 'best ask seen this tick' proxy, matching pong_resting_limit_study's own fill convention ('first subsequent bar whose LOW is strictly below the limit') and test_entry_manager.py's own tick-walk convention ('bar low = this tick's ask'). DISCLOSED: entry_manager.py is designed for live PER-SECOND tick sampling; this study necessarily discretizes to the coarser 5-min bar granularity the local OPRA cache provides -- 1 bar = 1 patience tick, a materially SLOWER patience clock than a live per-second actuator would run (a live build would resolve in seconds, not up to 15 minutes) -- named as a conservative-vs-optimistic open question in the build spec if this clears, not resolved here.
candidate_state_machine.patience_ticks_provenance: Reused UNCHANGED from shadow_entry_actuator.py's own already-frozen shadow-eval convention (delta=0.10, patience=3) -- not re-derived; delta_band is the swept axis around that same default (0.05/0.10/0.15).
candidate_state_machine.fill_price: state.limit_price EXACTLY on a FILLED resolution -- no added entry-side friction (the passive fill IS the honest price, matching pong-resting-limit's own no-double-count framing).
candidate_state_machine.convert_price: DISCLOSED DEVIATION from a literal plan_entry_action() single-ask-argument read: on a CONVERTED resolution (patience exhausted, policy='convert'), the realized entry price is NOT state.fill_price (which would reuse the SAME bar.low the fill-check tested against, double-dipping the bar's best price for a fallback that should be WORSE, not equally good) -- instead the candidate's convert price is bar.close + DEFAULT_ENTRY_SLIPPAGE (a realistic marketable price with the SAME real entry-side friction the control pays), computed on the SAME bar plan_entry_action resolved CONVERT on. This is a deliberate, disclosed correction of the naive reuse -- entry_manager's STATE TRANSITIONS (pending/filled/converted/missed + patience counting) are reused verbatim; only the CONVERT case's realized fill price is computed independently for honesty.
candidate_state_machine.cancel_or_missed_price: No trade -- candidate contributes pnl=0 for that episode in the delta-WF pairing (untraded side convention, matches WF-GATE-METHODOLOGY + pong precedent).

cancel_watcher.definition: REUSES pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17's own cancel-watcher CONCEPT (not code, since PONG's watcher is coupled to its own zone-arm mining loop): checked BEFORE each option-bar tick, over SPY bars from the trigger bar forward to the current option bar's timestamp -- if the underlying has traded through the signal's OWN trigger level by >= cancel_threshold (support: SPY.low <= L - threshold; resistance: SPY.high >= L + threshold), the resting order is canceled immediately (episode outcome = canceled_watcher, no trade), pre-empting the entry_manager state machine entirely for that tick onward -- avoiding chasing a real breakout the way PONG's own no_cancel control cell was shown to (74-81% raw slice-through).
cancel_watcher.none_purpose: the raw/uncanceled control cell for measuring adverse selection on THIS narrower, later-stage mechanism (does resting AFTER a trigger already fired see less adverse selection than PONG's before-trigger arming? -- an open empirical question this study answers).

mechanism_spec.adverse_selection_classification: Applied to every CANDIDATE-FILLED episode (filled or converted), REUSING pong-resting-limit's own frozen convention verbatim: up to 3 subsequent SPY 5m bars (15 min) after the fill bar; bounce = level held (no window bar breaches by >= $0.10); slice_through = the complement. Reported per cell, matching PONG's central-question framing ('the adverse-selection split front and center').

exit_grid._doc: FIXED, not swept -- exit shape is not the axis under test (entry mechanism is); matches SS-B-lineage / CLAUDE.md v15.3 chart-stop-primary doctrine.
exit_grid.stop_type: structure (structure_stop_study.structure_stop_signal_time against the SAME trigger level, buffer=STRUCTURE_BUFFER['SS-B']=0.0) with a -0.50 premium catastrophe backstop, always present -- matches live v15.3 chart-stop-primary + SS-B-lineage convention unchanged.
exit_grid.profit_lock_mode: trailing, trail_pct=0.15 -- SS_B_SHAPE unchanged, reused not re-derived.

mechanism_spec.one_position_at_a_time: Per account, per day: episodes are scoped per (date, level, role) exactly as control_outcome() already scopes them (no additional cross-level daily-slot state machine is introduced in this study -- unlike PONG, there is no PRE-TRIGGER arming step competing for a daily slot; each fired trigger is its own independent episode, matching how the live engine actually evaluates each setup opportunity).

friction.entry_side: NONE on the candidate's FILLED outcome (passive fill IS the honest price); the candidate's CONVERTED outcome DOES carry DEFAULT_ENTRY_SLIPPAGE (a real marketable price, honestly charged); the CONTROL carries DEFAULT_ENTRY_SLIPPAGE always (matches pong-resting-limit's own asymmetry, which is the whole point of the comparison).
friction.exit_side: BOTH candidate and control carry the standard house exit-side friction: DEFAULT_EXIT_SLIPPAGE=0.02 + DEFAULT_COMMISSION=0.65/contract/side (lib.simulator_credit, unchanged).
friction.no_double_count_statement: Same statement as pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17: only the CONVERTED candidate path and the control ever cross the spread on entry; the FILLED candidate path does not, by construction, and is not additionally charged.

ratification_gates._doc: Per CLAUDE.md OP-16 + WF-GATE-METHODOLOGY-2026-07-16.md (+ AMENDMENT 1), IDENTICAL form to pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17 -- re-applied, not re-derived. ALL FIVE required, per account, independently (C29).
ratification_gates.pairing_convention: delta_i = pnl_candidate(episode_i) - pnl_control(episode_i) over the union of episodes either side traded (untraded side contributes pnl=0).
ratification_gates.1_oos_positive: sum(delta_i for episodes with date >= oos_start) > 0.
ratification_gates.2_wf_ge_070: WF_delta = (sum_oos(delta_i)/n_oos) / (sum_is(delta_i)/n_is) >= 0.70, computed ONLY when is_delta_mean > 0 (frozen verdict ladder per AMENDMENT 1).
ratification_gates.3_sub_window_stable: OOS delta episodes split chronologically in half (sw1/sw2); <=1 of {sw1,sw2} negative.
ratification_gates.4_anchor_no_regression: None of the 6 CLAUDE.md/WF-lineage J-anchor trade dates (2026-04-29, 05-01, 05-04, 05-05, 05-06, 05-07 -- the SAME set pong-resting-limit-2026-07-17 and zone-rejection-band-2026-07-17 both use, reused unchanged) is touched by a candidate-side FILLED-or-CONVERTED episode in the delta population.
ratification_gates.5_evidence_n_advisory: n (episodes in the delta population, post exclusions) >= 15 is ADVISORY (OP-16) -- a thin-n PASS ships if the other 4 gates clear, labeled thin, not hidden.
ratification_gates.control_sanity_disclosure: A null/control sanity cell (candidate-vs-itself, guaranteed delta=0 for every episode by construction) is computed and reported, matching pong-resting-limit's own mandatory WF-GATE-METHODOLOGY disclosure.
ratification_gates.bh_fdr_correction: Benjamini-Hochberg step-up (autoresearch.ribbon_rejection_wick_battery.bh_fdr / FDR_ALPHA=0.10) across all 18 (delta_band x policy x cancel_watcher) test statistics PER ACCOUNT (36 total across both accounts, corrected independently per account per C29), one-sided normal-approximation p-value for mean(delta_i) > 0 against the house empirical null (autoresearch.null_baseline.random_entry_null). A cell failing the BH-FDR cut does NOT auto-ship even if conditions 1-5 nominally clear.

decision_rule.statement: Per account, independently: a (delta_band, policy, cancel_watcher) cell is SHIP-READY iff it clears all 5 ratification_gates AND survives BH-FDR. If >=1 cell is ship-ready on an account, the WINNER is the cell with the highest OOS delta expectancy per trade (tie-break: larger n). Per the task's explicit instruction, the adverse-selection split (bounce vs slice_through) is reported for the winner (and every cell) as a REPORTING requirement, not an additional numeric gate -- a technically-ship-ready cell whose edge is bounce-only and slice-negative still ships but must disclose that composition. SHIP timing (a live intent-type build in entry_manager.py's own shape) is separately gated on J review per the task's own 'write the BUILD SPEC, not the build' framing -- no entry_manager.py/j_intent_executor/params.json edit happens as part of this study or its scorecard regardless of outcome.
decision_rule.kill_criterion: If NO cell clears on EITHER account: KILL. Current immediate marketable-entry semantics stand. The scorecard reports the closest cell (most gates passed, tie-break least-negative OOS delta) and names the failing gate(s), PLUS the adverse-selection split regardless of outcome (measuring it is itself part of the deliverable). The scorecard ADDITIONALLY cross-references part (A)'s correlational finding explicitly: if (A) shows a real location/outcome correlation but (B) kills, the honest verdict is 'location matters, deliberate targeting via THIS mechanism does not capture it' -- not a blanket 'the wick was luck, full stop'.

outputs.build_spec_location: A section in the scorecard md (NOT a separate file), IF AND ONLY IF >=1 part (B) cell clears.

Part (B) is ANALYSIS ONLY over historical OPRA local cache -- no params.json/aggressive-params.json/filters.py/entry_manager.py/j_intent_executor edit happens inside the study script, no orders placed. Any BUILD (wiring entry_manager.py into a live intent path) is explicitly deferred to a SEPARATE, later, J-reviewed step -- this prereg and its study authorize evidence-gathering only.
